references.excerpt: Optimal care of critically ill patients in the cardiac intensive care unit includes adequate nutritional support. This review highlights the high prevalence of malnutrition in acute heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, cardiogenic shock, and post-cardiac arrest and its adverse impact on prognosis. Patients on extracorporeal life support (ECLS), either for respiratory or cardiac support, are at high risk of malnutrition.

cards.question: When should enteral nutrition be started in the critically ill?
cards.answer: Within 24–48 h of ICU admission once haemodynamically stable, even at trophic rates; early EN preserves gut mucosa and reduces infectious complications (ESPEN 2019, ASPEN/SCCM 2016).

cards.question: What energy and protein targets should be used in ICU?
cards.answer: Aim for 20–25 kcal/kg/day (ramp up from day 3–7) and 1.3 g/kg/day protein using actual body weight; indirect calorimetry is preferred when available to avoid over- and under-feeding.

cards.question: How is refeeding syndrome recognised and prevented?
cards.answer: Risk factors include BMI <16, >10 days starvation, low pre-feed K/Mg/PO₄; start at ≤10 kcal/kg/day, replace phosphate, potassium, magnesium and thiamine, and increase calories over 4–7 days while monitoring electrolytes daily.
